subject: AlphaEdge - Order Form: subcontracting clause change (flow-down checkpoint)
messages:
From: Ellis Cooper <ellis.cooper@alphaedge.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@alphaedge.com>, AlphaEdge Legal <legalops@alphaedge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form AE-42 - subcontracting clause update

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move ahead. Legal reviewed the draft Order Form and MSA and wants us to accept a tighter subcontracting/flow-down clause. Specifically, they asked that any downstream vendor that processes customer data be bound by the same DPA obligations and notify AlphaEdge within 10 business days of adding any new subprocessor. They attached a marked-up redline (AlphaEdge_Redlines_v3.docx) and a short evidence request matrix.

Can Redwood confirm you can:
- Add the 10-business-day notice requirement for new subprocessors,
- Commit to flow-down the DPA obligations to subprocessors, and
- Provide the requested certification/evidence for existing vendors (see matrix).

We know this is not standard for all customers — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through specifics. Our target signature date is 09/10; is that workable?

Best,
Ellis Cooper
Head of Procurement, AlphaEdge
ellis.cooper@alphaedge.com

Attachments: AlphaEdge_Redlines_v3.docx (redline), evidence_matrix.xlsx (list)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Cooper <ellis.cooper@alphaedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form AE-42 - subcontracting clause update

Hi Ellis — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. 

Short answers up front: we can generally support flow-down obligations to subprocessors and provide evidence for most standard integrations; the 10-business-day notification window is tighter than our usual practice but we can discuss an operational path.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal review between Legal + Ops (I’ve looped Karthik and Marissa) to confirm feasibility and identify any vendor exceptions.
2) A 30-minute checkpoint call between our legal ops and yours tomorrow or Wednesday to walk through the redline and the evidence matrix.
3) If we have any vendor-specific exceptions, we’ll produce a short deviation log and proposed mitigations (eg. contractual IOs or data-scoped exceptions).

Can you do a 30-min call Wed 08/31 at 10:00am PT? If not, suggest an alternate. We’ll prepare a short implementation matrix showing which vendors require additional paperwork and an estimated lead-time to collect artifacts.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Sales Operations (Redwood Inference)
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachment referenced: OrderForm_AE-42_20260829.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellis Cooper <ellis.cooper@alphaedge.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form AE-42 - subcontracting clause update

Grace / Marissa — quick internal notes before the call: 

Summary of my read on the redline (quick bullets):
- Flow-down of DPA obligations: we accept in principle; this aligns with our Private/VPC and Dedicated customers but requires vendor assessments for hosted integrations.
- Notification window: 10 business days is aggressive. Ops can often provide notification, but vendor contracts and onboarding processes can make tight windows infeasible for some legacy vendors (we have a handful of SaaS vendors with 30–60 day notice cycles).
- Evidence matrix: most evidence we have readily available (SOC2, DPA templates, processor lists) but collecting bespoke signed DPAs from downstream subvendors will take time for a subset.

Action items for the call:
- Marissa to prepare an implementation matrix (vendor / current contract / evidence available / estimated days to comply).
- Grace to confirm contract language tolerances (can we suggest 15 business days as a compromise?)
- I will flag any vendor-specific blocking items to Legal and propose mitigations (e.g., limited-scope carve-outs, transition timelines).

If AlphaEdge needs a firm 10-business-day commitment, we should be explicit about which vendor classes that applies to (redwood-managed infra vs third-party integrators).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Cooper <ellis.cooper@alphaedge.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form AE-42 - subcontracting clause update

Thanks everyone — notes from our 30-min checkpoint earlier today (call held 09/01 10:00am PT):

On the call: Ellis Cooper (AlphaEdge), Jordan Price (AlphaEdge Legal), Grace O'Connor (Redwood Sales Ops), Karthik Iyer (Redwood Legal Ops), Marissa Cole (Redwood Vendor Ops).

Key outcomes: 
- Redwood confirmed we will accept DPA flow-down obligations to subprocessors for this engagement, and we will produce an implementation matrix listing affected vendors and evidence types.
- We proposed a 15-business-day notification window as a pragmatic compromise; AlphaEdge asked for internal approval and will respond by 09/02 EOD.
- For a small set (~5 vendors) where contract terms prevent a 15-day notification, Redwood will provide compensating controls and a timeline to remediate (typical: 30–60 days).
- Marissa will deliver the vendor implementation matrix and the first tranche of artifacts (SOC2 reports, vendor DPAs we control) by 09/07.
- If AlphaEdge requires signed DPAs from downstream subcontractors not under our control, we will need to raise that as a scope exception under the Order Form and provide an escalation path.

Attachments sent after call: evidence_matrix.xlsx (requested list), updated redline notes (AlphaEdge_Redlines_v3.docx - our comments embedded).

Next steps: 
- AlphaEdge to confirm whether 15 business days is acceptable (deadline 09/02 EOD).
- Redwood to send implementation matrix by 09/07 and flag any vendor blocking items immediately.
- If agreement reached, Legal to incorporate agreed language into Order Form and circulate final for signature (target 09/10).

Marissa Cole
Vendor Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Phone: +1 650-555-0142
